data.title: Anagram Hunt
data.statement:
Several players each have a hand of letter tiles. Each player attempts to form a word using all the letters in their hand. Determine the winner(s).

<<Game mode>>

- The game mode is either {{high}} or {{low}}.

- In {{high}} mode, the best word is the valid word with the <<highest score>>.

- In {{low}} mode, the best word is the valid word with the <<lowest score>>.

<<How players choose their words>>

- Every player chooses from the dictionary a valid word.

- A word is <<valid>> for a player if it is an <<exact anagram>> of that player's hand: it must contain exactly the same letters with the same frequencies.

- If there are multiple valid words, the player chooses the <<lexicographically smallest>> among them.

- A player may have no valid word.

<<Determining the winner(s)>>

- Ignore any player who has no valid word.

- The <<score>> of a word is the sum of the standard English Scrabble tile values of its letters, as shown in the table below.

- Among the remaining players, compare the scores of their words and determine the winning score based on the game mode ({{high}} = highest, {{low}} = lowest).

- Every player whose word has the winning score is a winner. There may be multiple winners.

- The winners' names and their winning words are output in the same order in which the players appear in the input.

<<Letter scoring>>

The standard English Scrabble tile values are:
```
 1 point : a, e, i, l, n, o, r, s, t, u
 2 points: d, g
 3 points: b, c, m, p
 4 points: f, h, v, w, y
 5 points: k
 8 points: j, x
10 points: q, z
```

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

Several players each have a hand of letter tiles. Each player attempts to form a word using all the letters in their hand. Determine the winner(s).

Game mode

- The game mode is either high or low.

- In high mode, the best word is the valid word with the highest score.

- In low mode, the best word is the valid word with the lowest score.

How players choose their words

- Every player chooses from the dictionary a valid word.

- A word is valid for a player if it is an exact anagram of that player's hand: it must contain exactly the same letters with the same frequencies.

- If there are multiple valid words, the player chooses the lexicographically smallest among them.

- A player may have no valid word.

Determining the winner(s)

- Ignore any player who has no valid word.

- The score of a word is the sum of the standard English Scrabble tile values of its letters, as shown in the table below.

- Among the remaining players, compare the scores of their words and determine the winning score based on the game mode (high = highest, low = lowest).

- Every player whose word has the winning score is a winner. There may be multiple winners.

- The winners' names and their winning words are output in the same order in which the players appear in the input.

Letter scoring

The standard English Scrabble tile values are:

 1 point : a, e, i, l, n, o, r, s, t, u
 2 points: d, g
 3 points: b, c, m, p
 4 points: f, h, v, w, y
 5 points: k
 8 points: j, x
10 points: q, z





   

      
Input

      
Line 1: mode (high or low)
Line 2: n (number of scrambled groups)
Next n lines: name hand (space-separated)
Line after: d (dictionary size)
Next d lines: dictionary words

   

   

      
Output

      
One line per winning player, in the same order they appeared in the input: name word. There is always at least one winning player.

   

   

      
Constraints

      
1 ≤ n ≤ 10
1 ≤ d ≤ 30
1 ≤ length of each hand/word ≤ 12
mode = high or low
Player names are unique, lowercase, no spaces
At least one player is guaranteed to have a valid (anagram-matching) word

   

   

      
Example

      

         

            
Input

            
high
2
alice tac
bob xof
3
cat
dog
fox

         

         

            
Output

            
bob fox
